The app builds successfully. Here's what was created:

**Architecture: Blazor Web App with Auto render mode** — pages render via Server on first visit (fast load), then switch to WebAssembly for subsequent interactions (no server round-trips for worldwide users).

**Project structure:**

| Component | Location |
|---|---|
| Shared models & service interface | `ShipmentTracker.Client/Models/`, `Client/Services/IShipmentService.cs` |
| WASM HTTP service | `Client/Services/ClientShipmentService.cs` |
| Server DB service | `ShipmentTracker/Services/ServerShipmentService.cs` |
| Dispatch dashboard (auth-required) | `Client/Pages/Shipments.razor` |
| Customer tracking page (public) | `Client/Pages/TrackShipment.razor` |
| REST API for WASM client | Minimal API in `Program.cs` |
| EF Core + SQLite + seed data | `Data/ApplicationDbContext.cs`, migration auto-applied |

**Key features:**
- **Dispatchers** — filter/search shipments, change statuses, create new shipments (login required)
- **Customers** — track by number with progress bar, estimated delivery countdown (no login needed)
- **Individual accounts** via ASP.NET Identity (registration, login, account management)
- **5 seed shipments** with realistic international routes
- **`InteractiveAuto`** render mode on all interactive pages

Run with: `cd ShipmentTracker && dotnet run --project ShipmentTracker`
